newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir tells Malaysians to avoid "greedy" label.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir tells Malaysians to avoid "greedy" label.

text.p: Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has advised Malaysians to be cautious when investing in nations such as the Philippines to avoid being branded as "greedy", the national Bernama news agency reported on Sunday.
Commenting on a court ruling which barred Malaysia's Renong Bhd from buying a historical hotel in the Philippines, Mahathir said Malaysians could make their investments elsewhere.
"I feel Malaysian investors will be more careful and will not invest too much in the Philippines," Mahathir was quoted as saying by Bernama.
"We do not want others to say we are very greedy to the extent of wanting to grab all the investments for ourselves," he said.
The Philippine Supreme Court decided last week to stop the Philippine Government from selling Manila Hotel, a national monument, to Renong, which won a bid to acquire the hotel in 1995.
The court ordered that the hotel be sold to the Manila-based Prince Hotel Corporation in line with the "Filipinos-come-first policy".
Mahathir declined to comment on whether the court ruling would strain bilateral ties.
He, however, said he believed the recent turnaround of the Philippine economy may prompt the country -- once very liberal to Malaysian investors -- to change its outlook to foreign investment.
"I feel due to the recovery, certainly there will be a slight shift in Philippine view towards foreign investment," he said.
